name: GTM Outreach — 1) Scrape, Enrich, Personalize, Send

parameters.jsCode:
const job = $('Pick Decision Maker').item.json;
const raw = ($input.item.json.data || '') + '';
const site = raw
  .replace(/<script[\s\S]*?<\/script>/gi, ' ')
  .replace(/<style[\s\S]*?<\/style>/gi, ' ')
  .replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ' ')
  .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')
  .slice(0, 4000);
const profile = $('Load Profile').first().json.stdout;
const firstName = (job.contact_name || '').split(' ')[0] || 'there';
const jd = (job.job_description || '').replace(/visit link.*/i,'').trim();
const prompt = `You are writing ONE cold email for Arsal, an OUTBOUND go-to-market (GTM) engineer, to ${firstName} (${job.contact_title}) at ${job.company}, which is HIRING a ${job.position}.
Arsal IS interested in that role. This email is a direct, proactive application: instead of dropping a resume into the ATS, he reaches out to the decision-maker and shows what he'd actually build for them. Earn a reply by being relevant and useful, not by asking for a job.

WHO ARSAL IS: a GTM engineer who builds the SYSTEM behind outbound revenue — not one-off campaigns, but reliable, modular, always-on infrastructure that ties a company's fragmented GTM stack (Clay, Apollo/ZoomInfo, the CRM, the sequencer) into one coherent engine. He brings engineering discipline so it stays maintainable and does not break as they scale: automated list-building + CRM enrichment, AI personalization at the company level, multi-domain cold-email infrastructure with deliverability (SPF/DKIM/DMARC), lead scoring/routing, and signal/trigger-based outreach that replaces manual SDR work. Outbound-focused and systems-minded — the opposite of a tactical lead-gen hack.

PRIMARY INTELLIGENCE = THE JOB DESCRIPTION. Read it first. It reveals the gap they want this role to own, the tools/stack they already run (Clay, Apollo, Outreach, Smartlead, HubSpot, Salesforce, Instantly...), and their outbound maturity. Build the email from that. If JD is thin, infer from role title + site, stay outbound.

=== DATA ===
ROLE: ${job.position}
JOB DESCRIPTION (primary): ${jd ? jd.slice(0, 2800) : '(not available - infer from role + site)'}
COMPANY: ${job.company} (${job.company_website || 'website unknown'})
WEBSITE TEXT (secondary): ${site || '(unavailable)'}
DECISION MAKER: ${job.contact_name}, ${job.contact_title}

=== ARSAL PROFILE (use only real facts) ===
${profile}

=== HARD CONTENT RULES ===
1. STRICTLY OUTBOUND. Never pitch inbound tactics — no website-visitor de-anonymization, no RB2B, no "track who visits your site", no site-intent capture.
2. NEVER pitch the company something their own product already does, and never pitch what they obviously already have.
3. The HOOK insight must be RELEVANT to what they're hiring this role to fix (from the JD) or a real gap in their OUTBOUND motion. If it could be sent to any company, rewrite it.
4. The PLAY = one concrete GTM-engineering move tailored to the gap, framed as a SYSTEM not a hack: something that integrates their existing tools, runs reliably and always-on, and removes manual work as they scale (e.g. a modular Clay enrichment + personalization layer feeding their sequencer, an automated signal-triggered outbound engine, standardizing/cleaning their CRM data so campaigns stop breaking, fixing deliverability across sending domains). Show systems thinking — reliable, maintainable, integrated — not just 'send more emails'. Pick the highest-leverage move for THEM; never reuse one template across companies.
5. Back it with Arsal's real experience lightly; never brag or dump numbers. If Arsal has run outbound in the TARGET company's industry (his client/industry list is in the profile above), reference it briefly as proof — e.g. "I've built outbound systems for recruiting firms before" or "...for construction companies before". Match by industry, keep it natural and true, and don't force it or name a client that doesn't fit. When a case study in the profile matches their industry, you MAY cite ONE concrete result from it as quiet proof (e.g. "for a construction client, cold outbound booked 20 calls in the first month" or "for a fintech I helped drive ~$1M in 90 days") — exactly one number, woven in naturally, never a list. If that matching case study has a shareable link in the profile, you MAY include that one link as proof.

=== STRUCTURE (5 short parts, in this order) ===
1) OPENER (1 sentence): acknowledge their open ${job.position} role and that you're reaching out directly rather than vanishing into the applicant pile. Casual, self-aware, a little confident — never desperate. VARY the wording each time (e.g. "Saw you're hiring a ${job.position} — figured a direct note beats another resume in the stack." or "Noticed the ${job.position} opening; the useful stuff never fits in a resume, so reaching out here instead."). This sets up why you're emailing.
2) HOOK (1 sentence): a specific insight or gap rooted in ≥2 verifiable facts about this company (their tool stack from the JD, team size, funding stage, a named initiative). Must be impossible to send unchanged to a different company.
3) PLAY (2 sentences): the concrete outbound move, mechanism named.
4) CREDIBILITY (1 sentence): light proof, e.g. "I've built these outbound systems before."
5) CTA: soft two-choice question first that defers scheduling to them — e.g. “Would a quick 15-min call this week work?” Then on a new line the booking link as a convenience: “Grab a slot: https://calendly.com/arsal4527/gtm-strategy” Always give an easy off-ramp — e.g. “Happy to reconnect when timing is better.” Never open with the link.
Sign off with the name/style from Arsal profile.

=== TONE BAR EXAMPLE (match the human tone and specificity; do NOT copy its wording or structure verbatim) ===
Leo,
Saw you're hiring a GTM engineer — figured a direct note would land better than another resume in the pile.
Your post lists Clay and Smartlead but mentions reps still building lists by hand, which usually means the outbound engine stalls whenever someone gets busy.
One move: a Clay workflow that auto-builds and enriches your ICP lists from intent triggers, writes the first line per lead, and drops them into Smartlead, so list-building stops being a person's full-time job.
I've built these outbound systems before. Happy to map what it'd look like for your stack.
If it's worth 15 minutes, grab a slot: https://calendly.com/arsal4527/gtm-strategy
Best,
Arsal

=== STYLE RULES ===
- 90 to 140 words. Plain text. First name. Contractions, short lines, plain words.
- BANNED: "I hope this finds you well", "I wanted to reach out", "I came across", "excited", "passionate", "leverage", "synergy", "fast-paced", "game-changer", "delve", "robust", "seamless", "elevate", "unlock", "spearhead", corporate/AI filler. No stacked dashes, no tidy three-part lists.
- NEVER start the email body with “I” as the first word — open with the recipient’s name or a company-specific observation.
- Max ONE question per email. Confident but not arrogant.
- Do NOT say a resume is attached; a resume link is added automatically below your signature.

Also produce: gtm_insights = 3 short specific observations about their OUTBOUND/GTM and stack; one_liner = the custom outbound play in one sentence.

SUBJECT LINE: write it like a real person emailing a peer, NOT a marketer. 3 to 7 words, lowercase, casual and specific — 4 to 5 words is the sweet spot. The kind of internal-looking note someone actually opens.
GOOD vibe: "your outbound setup", "quick idea for ${job.company}", "${job.company} cold outreach", "the manual list problem", "your gtm hire", "outbound idea".
NEVER: title case, exclamation marks, emojis, colons, hype ("Unlock Pipeline Growth"), generic ("Quick question"), or application-style ("Application for GTM Engineer"). If it sounds like a marketing email or a tool generated it, rewrite it.

Return ONLY valid JSON, no markdown, no code fences:
{"gtm_insights":["...","...","..."],"one_liner":"...","email_subject":"...","email_body":"..."}`;
return { json: { ...job, prompt } };

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ model: $('Config').first().json.model, max_tokens: 1500, messages: [{ role: 'user', content: $json.prompt }] }) }}

const cfg = $('Config').first().json;
const job = $('Finalize Attachment').item.json;
const gm = $input.item.json || {};
const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
return { json: {
  date: today,
  company: job.company || '',
  position: job.position || '',
  location: job.location || '',
  job_url: job.url || '',
  company_headcount: (job.company_headcount || '') + '',
  company_website: job.company_website || '',
  company_linkedin: job.company_linkedin_real || job.company_linkedin || '',
  contact_name: job.contact_name || '',
  contact_title: job.contact_title || '',
  contact_email: job.contact_email || '',
  contact_linkedin: job.contact_linkedin || '',
  one_liner: job.one_liner || '',
  gtm_insights: job.gtm_insights || '',
  email_subject: job.email_subject || '',
  status: cfg.send_mode === 'send' ? 'sent' : 'drafted',
  thread_id: gm.threadId || (gm.message && gm.message.threadId) || '',
  message_id: gm.id || (gm.message && gm.message.id) || '',
  followups: 0,
  last_touch: today,
} };

const j = $input.item.json;
const today = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
return { json: {
  date: today,
  company: j.company || '',
  position: j.position || '',
  location: j.location || '',
  job_url: j.url || '',
  company_headcount: (j.company_headcount || '') + '',
  company_website: j.company_website || '',
  company_linkedin: j.company_linkedin_real || j.company_linkedin || '',
  contact_name: j.contact_name || '',
  contact_title: j.contact_title || '',
  contact_email: '',
  contact_linkedin: j.contact_linkedin || '',
  one_liner: '',
  gtm_insights: '',
  email_subject: '',
  status: j.skip_reason || 'skipped',
  thread_id: '',
  message_id: '',
  followups: 0,
  last_touch: today,
} };
